reason: Under the comparison heading, the quotes state AWS recommends RDS as the default choice for most relational deployments and that the on-premises and EC2 alternatives make you spend more time managing software and hardware.
The quote states accounts have a default VPC and all new DB instances are created in it unless you specify otherwise.
The What's New quotes state pause, resume to a log position and promote, faster recovery than point-in-time restore which can take hours for large databases, posted Aug 22, 2025.

The quotes support restoring from a final snapshot and that without one no final snapshot exists; the claim's 'you can restore only from retained automated backups or an earlier manual snapshot' comes from an unquoted context sentence, and 'only' is stronger than its 'either ... or' wording.
The quotes state automated backups are deleted with the instance unless Retain automated backups is chosen, and final and manual snapshots are independent and not deleted.
The quote states same-Region automated backups are deleted if not retained, but backups replicated to another Region are kept.
The quotes state deletion protection is on by default for console-created instances, must be off before deleting, and turning it off does not cause an outage.
The quotes state a database on EC2 is more prone to user errors and manual OS or database software updates might cause application downtime.
Under Benefits, the quote states Cross-AZ ENA Express reduces replication latency and its variability and improves failover reliability for write-intensive workloads.

The quote supports enabled by default on new Multi-AZ instances with eligible classes; the three ways to enable it on an existing instance (stop/start, modify class, Scale Compute) appear only in unquoted context.
The quotes state RDS supports Cross-AZ ENA Express for eligible classes in Multi-AZ deployments and it increases single-flow bandwidth for faster block-level replication between primary and standby.
The quote states verbatim that Cross-AZ ENA Express is not supported for RDS for SQL Server.
The quote describes snapshot, copy with a KMS key to encrypt the copy, then restore an encrypted DB instance.
The quotes state AES-256, transparent access authentication and decryption with minimal performance impact, and no client application changes.
The quotes state availability for all engines and storage types and for most instance classes; the page table lists M1, M2 and db.t2.micro as unsupported, matching the condition.
The quote lists underlying storage, logs, automated backups, read replicas and snapshots as encrypted at rest.
The quote states a blue/green deployment can create a green environment with a different KMS key to encrypt an unencrypted instance or change the key.
The quotes state you can't turn off encryption and you can export data and import it into an unencrypted instance.
The quote states RDS uses the AWS managed key when no customer managed key is specified, with a different AWS managed key per Region.

The quotes support losing key access on disable and the terminal state after seven days with restore only from snapshot or backup; the recovery steps (enable key and restart) and the recoverable state with its backups-enabled and can-stop conditions are only in unquoted context.
The quotes support that the key can't be changed and the snapshot-copy workaround; the claim's 'or use a blue/green deployment' is not in any quote of this fact.
The quote states KMS keys are Region-specific and a cross-Region read replica needs a key in the destination Region.
The quotes state you can't create an encrypted snapshot of an unencrypted instance and an encrypted instance's snapshot uses the same KMS key.
The quote supports the restriction, but the claim's added step 'you first make an encrypted copy of the snapshot' is not in the quote.
The quotes state encryption only at creation and that encrypting a snapshot copy effectively adds encryption.
The quotes state no encrypted replica of unencrypted or vice versa, and same-Region encrypted replicas use the source's KMS key.
The quote states replication traffic to read replicas is encrypted for encrypted and unencrypted instances, even across Regions.
The quote states TDE support for Oracle and SQL Server, combinable with encryption at rest with a possible slight performance effect, and different keys per method.
The quote states engine upgrades require downtime and a blue/green deployment can minimize it.
The quote lists IBM Db2, MariaDB, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle Database and PostgreSQL.
The quotes state real-time OS monitoring useful for per-process CPU use, agent versus hypervisor sourcing, and delivery to CloudWatch Logs.
The quotes state Performance Insights assesses database load and Enhanced Monitoring looks at real-time OS metrics.

The quotes support event categories and the SNS topic ARN per subscription; the list of resource types (instances, snapshots, parameter groups, security groups, RDS Proxy) is not in any quote or its context.
The quote states rules match RDS events and choose automated actions, with targets such as a Lambda function or an SNS topic.
The quotes state all snapshot types (manual, automated, AWS Backup) can be exported and the bucket must be in the snapshot's Region.
The quote states exported data can be analyzed directly with Athena or Redshift Spectrum.
The quote states exported data can't be restored to a new instance or imported into an existing one.
The quotes state export to S3 in compressed Apache Parquet, running in the background without affecting the active database.
The quote states RDS auto-enrolls instances and clusters in Extended Support after end of standard support unless disabled at creation or restore.

The quote supports that the charge stops automatically on 'one of the following actions', but the two actions (upgrade to a standard-support version, delete the database) are only in the unquoted bullet list.
